source.title: Optimal Machine Intelligence Near the Edge of Chaos
source.authors: Ling Feng; Lin Zhang; C. Lai

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and figure captions; figures themselves are not rendered.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains image-classification networks and measures test performance alongside dynamical stability, but it does not measure training classification error as the claim versions define it. Its accuracy results and qualitative training-error descriptions address related training behavior with different measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracies in tables and describes training/test accuracy patterns for selected plots. It does not report numeric training classification errors. Jacobian norms, asymptotic distances, and their phase assignments are not outcomes measuring the claim's training-error behavior. The cited methods and prior results are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether classification performance correlates with asymptotic dynamical stability. Its test accuracies and stability measures do not establish any claim version. Training-accuracy curves are mentioned, but the supplied text gives no readable endpoint establishing near-zero training error. There are no relevant initialization, shortcut, normalization, or learning-rate comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors associate optimal test performance with proximity to the edge of chaos and observe training trajectories approaching it. DenseNet40 can remain chaotic; weight decay and dropout move it toward the boundary and reduce the generalization gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains image-classification networks with Adam and evaluates test accuracy and asymptotic stability; it does not use the claim versions' interventions or training-error measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported stability behavior varies with architecture depth and regularization: DenseNet40 remains chaotic after long training, while weight decay and dropout move it toward the edge of chaos.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors associate lowest test loss and saturating test accuracy with proximity to the edge of chaos in MLPs and CNNs; ResNet and DenseNet generally move toward that boundary during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classification performance during training is associated with proximity to an asymptotic dynamical boundary in the extracted network operator.

fits_no_version.finding: DenseNet40 remains chaotic after prolonged training; weight decay and dropout move it toward the boundary and reduce the training-test accuracy gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization can change asymptotic input dynamics and reduce the generalization gap without materially changing test accuracy.

record.problems: The text gives no numeric training classification errors for these findings. Many stability results are presented in figures; error bars are described for some plots but do not provide training-error measurements. The study uses CIFAR10 and Fashion MNIST, not CIFAR-100 or corrupted/random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figures S4–S9 report or illustrate classification accuracy and stability; the supplied text does not provide recoverable numeric values for the plotted accuracy series, and the stability measures do not measure the versions' claimed training-error outcomes.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100; random or corrupted labels; size, early-stopping, and regularization effects on training error.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and additional student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss recovery, curvature evolution, and optimization divergence.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The listed rows accurately reproduce the tables but supply no evidence for V1–V6. The stability findings require the text and figures, rather than the table accuracy values alone. Figure-only accuracy series are already declared in rows_left_out; their unavailable values do not justify inferring near-zero training error. Dynamical divergence under repeated application of a fixed network is distinct from divergence of parameter training.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, zero or near-zero error, corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size or early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual shortcut training-error comparisons and the cited special-initialization or normalization-free recipes.
Comparisons of initialization methods, training speed by initialization, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalized versus unnormalized training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.
